nodes.name: tree-model
nodes.summary: The stack learns to be an outline
nodes.body: stackTree replaces the rail layout: the stack stays a linearization (landing order is the spine), and dependency structure becomes indentation — a change nests under its deepest dependency (git-nearest on ties), diamond arms beyond the tree edge are kept as annotations, and every row carries its 1-based landing position so grouping by structure never loses the order. File-tree guide columns and elbow flags are computed here, pure and tested; malformed forward/self/unknown deps are dropped so the tree cannot cycle.

nodes.name: tree-view
nodes.summary: Graph mode grows rings, not wires
nodes.body: The rail rendering answered no user question, so tree mode now draws the outline the stacked-PR world settled on: full-width cards indented under what they build on, guide lines and elbows like a file tree, a #n landing-position badge per row, clickable "+ needs" chips for diamond arms (labels truncate, tooltips keep the evidence), and lineage coloring that only adds — upstream accent, downstream graph-5, nothing dimmed into looking disabled. The toggle reads List | Tree; the legacy graph preference maps to tree.
